timeline_utc.finding: Harness omitted list from both directory scopes. input had read_ai; output had read_ai/create_file. Product correctly denied directory listing.
Normal scope update added list to the same task after 9 model calls. Prior execution time remained charged.
Following native approval, one PUT returned 201 for output/project-summary.md: 453 bytes, approved content matched, no overwrite.
The model claimed input/progress.md remained 212 bytes in its directory verification. At this time its post-write tool trace had listed output only. This temporal/procedural claim lacked evidence.
The server verifier independently re-listed the input directory and passed the original observation comparison. This occurred AFTER the candidate final.

The server verifier re-read the input fragment and passed version/range/content comparison. All five mechanical checks ultimately passed; this does not retroactively establish what the model had checked before its candidate final.

Checker reported the unsupported post-write input directory claim. Its statement that input was not re-observed must be interpreted relative to the original candidate final, since the later server mechanical recheck did occur. One bounded correction continuation was scheduled.
Model performed a fresh input listing showing 212 bytes.
Model re-read input; content version matched the original.
A final correction inference began, but no subsequent verification completed.
The 600-second runtime deadline stopped execution with agent_time_limit. This was not an 18-call allowance exhaustion.

saved_deliverable.limitation: Saved/opened artifact success cannot replace task-level failed/unverified.

limits_and_usage.explanation: Runtime elapsed_seconds counts the whole claimed worker tick, including preparation/validation; budget active_seconds sums narrower model/tool dispatch intervals. The public archived task omitted runtime elapsed_seconds, so its exact historical value and detailed overhead breakdown cannot be reconstructed from the available public evidence. Neither the 128-call lifetime limit nor the 3600-second lifetime limit triggered this failure.

attribution.harness: Initial missing list permission caused the initial resource-access blockage. No product authorization bypass or grant defect established.
attribution.model_behavior: Repeated unproductive probes and an unsupported temporal verification statement were observed GLM choices. Checker inference took approximately 119 seconds. A different future model trajectory is not guaranteed by deterministic product fixes.
attribution.confirmed_product_usability_gap: The UI showed narrower call time as execution time while omitting the actual per-run deadline counter and limit. The run_timing change exposes these separately without modifying admission, budgets, stopping behavior or historical verdicts.
attribution.repair_feedback_projection_gap: At audit time repair feedback contained check statuses and evidence IDs but omitted the corresponding mechanical checked_at/facts/coverage. Supplying bounded current-cycle evidence could support a truthful correction; it must not turn post-final evidence into proof that the original statement was justified. This is a separate implementation/review workstream, not part of the timing fix.

boundaries.required_future_evidence: A fresh authorized native file-generation task must independently complete its write, openable artifact and verified task outcome. Deterministic timing tests and unrelated verified tasks do not establish that end-to-end success.
